# Give the model (fallback chain) config control over the free-tier request budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want to set the free-tier request-budget behaviour
**per model / fallback chain** (with sensible global defaults), so I can tune
`plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` independently — instead of every model
inheriting one global setting — while any single provider entry can still
override its own behaviour.

## Current state

- `rate_limit_rpm` is a **provider-entry** field (`provider_cfg`), so it is
  already configurable per entry — today only `munitoai-free` sets it (10).
- The four *behaviour* knobs are read **server-wide only**:
  `server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`,
  `server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py::_config_value`, called with the server
  config).
- `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id, request)` is **not**
  given `model_config`/the model name, so a model-scoped setting cannot be
  expressed today — a single reserve ratio / wait cap applies to all chains.
- `affinity_ttl_seconds` is applied in three places, all of which read the same
  server config today: `acquire_provider_budget()`,
  `record_provider_affinity()` (via `provider.py::_maybe_record_provider_affinity`)
  and `provider_affinity_active()`. Honouring a model-scoped TTL (AC1) therefore
  requires threading the model config into the affinity record/lookup path too,
  not only into the acquire call.
- Both budget call sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` are
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8141); each already holds the request's
  `model_config`.
- Consequence: an interactive chain (e.g. `plan`) and a background chain (e.g.
  `compact`) cannot trade latency against free-tier utilisation differently, and
  a future gated entry cannot be tuned without changing global behaviour.
- Caveat on `compact`: `models.compact` is consumed only by
  `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, which dispatches to its providers
  directly over httpx and never calls the gate. A `models.compact.budget` block
  is therefore accepted and resolvable but has **no runtime effect** until that
  dispatch is gated (tracked separately — see OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Desired change

Add a **model-level `budget` block** with precedence
**provider entry > model block > server default > built-in default**:

```yaml
models:
  plan:
    budget:
      reserve_ratio: 0.4        # share of rate_limit_rpm reserved for in-progress
      wait_max_seconds: 10      # per-request wait cap for in-progress sessions
      max_waiters: 4            # concurrent waiter cap
      affinity_ttl_seconds: 600 # how long a session counts as in-progress
    providers:
      - name: munitoai-free
        rate_limit_rpm: 15      # entry-level override of the budget size
        budget:                 # optional per-entry behaviour override
          reserve_ratio: 0.2
```

- All five keys are optional at every layer; absent keys fall through to the next
  layer, so **existing configs behave exactly as today**.
- Values are clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today
  (ratio to `[0,1]`, wait/TTL to `>= 0`, malformed values fall back to the
  default with a warning — fail open, never fail closed).
- The effective values are visible per request in the budget logs/attempt
  diagnostics (which layer supplied `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`), and the
  provider diagnostics table keeps showing remaining/limit per entry.
- The budget **bucket** remains keyed by provider entry (one account quota shared
  by `plan`/`author`/`code` even when their model blocks differ) — document this
  explicitly so per-model tuning is not mistaken for per-model quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `models.<name>.budget` block is honoured for `reserve_ratio`,
   `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters` and `affinity_ttl_seconds`, and a provider
   entry may override any of them with its own `budget` block.
2. Precedence is exactly entry > model > server > built-in default, proven by
   tests for every key (single-layer and multi-layer combinations).
3. Omitting all blocks reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte — identical
   `BudgetDecision` values (`reserve_slots`, `effective_limit`, `reason`) and
   identical log lines for the shipped `config.yaml` (no behavioural change;
   tested).
4. Malformed/out-of-range values fall back to the next layer with a logged
   warning and never raise or block a request (tests for each key).
5. The budget bucket stays shared per provider entry across models; a test proves
   two models with different `budget` blocks still consume one `rate_limit_rpm`
   window.
6. The effective configuration is visible in the budget skip/wait log lines and
   the attempt diagnostics (source layer included), and the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
7. Tests cover both real fallback entry points —
   `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` —
   proving each passes the request's model config into the gate. (The intake's
   third clause, "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same
   gate", is **not implementable as written**: `models.compact` is consumed only
   by `build_compact_summarizer()`, which calls providers directly over httpx
   and never reaches the gate. See OPEN QUESTION 1 and the follow-up item.)
8. Documentation updated: `proxy/config.yaml` header comments + a commented
   example, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (model-level `budget` block alongside the `providers` list).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config-shape only: no change to gate semantics, reserve maths, or the
  affinity/wait design.
- Keep every layer optional; no migration of existing configs required.
- Do not introduce per-model *quota* (a separate budget per model) — that would
  break the one-account-per-entry model; if it is ever wanted, it must be a
  separate decision.
- The gate must remain fail-open when the new blocks are absent or malformed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — resolve each knob through the new
  entry > model > server precedence; extend `BudgetDecision`/logs with the source
  layer.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass `model_config` (and the model key) into
  `acquire_provider_budget()` from both fallback entry points
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`) and into
  `_maybe_record_provider_affinity()` so the recorded TTL matches the model.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — precedence/validation/shared-bucket
  tests, plus the call-site wiring test (the module already imports
  `proxy.provider as provider`, so no new test module is needed).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — document the `models.<name>.budget` block; commented
  example.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + fixtures — only if the new keys are
  introduced as shipped values (they are optional; likely no fixture change).
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — docs.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Add failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` for precedence,
   validation/fallback and the shared-bucket guarantee (AC1–AC5).
2. Implement the layered resolver in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
   (entry > model > server > built-in) and extend `BudgetDecision`/log lines
   with the source layer (AC6).
3. Thread `model_config` through both `provider.py` call sites and the affinity
   record/lookup path (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`, AC7).
4. Update docs: `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/README.md`,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (AC8).
5. Run the suite via the test skill (AC9).

## OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **Compaction/summarizer path and the budget gate.** AC7 originally asked for
   coverage of "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same gate".
   Fact check (this session): `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
   (`build_compact_summarizer` / `_remote_chat_url`) resolves
   `models.compact.providers` itself and calls each provider **directly over
   httpx**, bypassing `localhost:8080` — so it never reaches
   `acquire_provider_budget()` and no `budget` block applies to it.
   AC7 was therefore narrowed to the two real fallback entry points and the gap
   was filed as `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (Gate the models.compact summarizer
   dispatch through the provider budget).
   **Preferred option (a): accept the split** — it preserves the "config-shape
   only" constraint and leaves eight of nine ACs unblocked; the summarizer gate
   is tracked separately. Alternative (b): widen this item to gate the
   summarizer dispatch as well (larger effort, and the `compact` half of the
   user story only becomes real then). Producer decision requested — see the
   comment on this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is `rate_limit_rpm` used for any other provider (would per-model tuning
  matter beyond the free tier)?" Answer (Map, 2026-10-18, comment
  `LP-C0MVDVL1IR002EH5X`): no — `munitoai-free` is the only entry declaring it;
  the capability is dormant for every other provider, and the bucket is keyed by
  provider entry so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window.
- Q: "Do both `provider.py` budget call sites have `model_config` available, and
  what are the functions called?" Answer (this session, code inspection): yes —
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8145); the AC7 name `_proxy_with_fallback`
  was corrected accordingly.
- OPEN QUESTION 1 (compaction/summarizer gate) — see above; needs a producer
  decision before the item is implemented. It does not block the other eight
  ACs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s wait cap (introduced the knobs this item
  makes per-model).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — evaluating whether the `munitoai-free` budget itself
  should be raised (the first consumer of per-model tuning).
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — restricting the free tier to cheap mode (another
  model-scoped policy that could share this configuration shape).
- `LP-0MVDUZ0E10011W3C` (in progress) — rewrites the limiter/budget skip log
  lines that AC6 extends; sequence with it so the two log changes do not
  conflict.
- `LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY` (open) — consolidating the fallback-chain configuration
  docs, of which the `budget` block docs (AC8) are one part.
- `LP-0MVF2DNCX003Z5CO` (in progress) — per-model context size, an existing
  example of a model-level knob read per request.
- Follow-up (filed this session) — `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` — gate the
  `models.compact` summarizer dispatch so a `budget` block has runtime effect
  there.
data.title: Give the model/fallback-chain config control over free-tier budget knobs

# Intake Brief: Install the `.githooks/pre-push` gate (core.hooksPath) so the dev-push full-suite gate actually runs

**Headline:** This checkout runs **no** pre-push hook at all (`core.hooksPath` unset, `.git/hooks/pre-push` absent), and the committed hook is the framework **v2** variant which has **no full-suite test gate** — so a red tree can reach `dev`. Close the gap by activating the hook, adding a scope-aware full-suite gate to llm's `.githooks/pre-push` (runner resolved repo-local → global skill path), an idempotent installer, and documentation.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` intentionally defers full-suite testing to the dev-push integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81): the `.githooks/pre-push` hook is supposed to run `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on pushes to `dev`/`main`. In this llm checkout neither half is in place:

1. `git config core.hooksPath` is **unset** and `.git/hooks/pre-push` is absent — no hook is invoked at all (verified 2026-10-20).
2. The committed `.githooks/pre-push` is the framework **v2** hook (worklog sync + branch policy + context-budget gate) — it contains **no** full-suite test gate. The v3 gate with the suite gate exists only in SorraAgents and hard-requires a repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, which llm does not ship.

Consequence (evidence in ticket): `implement.py finish` pushed commit `2f922ab9` to `dev` in under a second with no suite execution; the full-suite cache entry appeared only after a manual `run_tests.py --scope full` run.

## Users / stakeholders

- **Framework/agent operators** pushing work to `dev` via `implement.py finish` or `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` — they rely on the push gate to catch full-suite regressions before `dev` is polluted.
- **Audit/verification consumers** (audit runner, post-push verification) that read the full-suite cache entry produced by the gate — a green `dev` after a push is only trustworthy if the gate ran.
- **SorraAgents framework maintainers** — the canonical v3 gate and its docs (SorraAgents repo) are the reference design; llm's fix must stay consistent with the documented per-project policy.

Example user story: "As an operator finishing work item F2, I push to `dev` via `implement.py finish`; a suite-breaking change must be refused at the push so `dev` never holds a red tree, and a feature-branch push must not be slowed by a full-suite run."

## Acceptance Criteria

Pending producer decisions in the Appendix (Q1–Q3); draft wording below reflects the recommended option and updates the original ACs to match reality:

1. **Gate active:** the checkout has the pre-push gate active via an idempotent install (e.g. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` set by a committed installer script), effective for the main checkout and its worktrees.
2. **Full-suite gate on dev push:** a test push to `dev` with a deliberately failing test is **refused** by the hook (verified once, then reverted). The gate runs the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`) when the push targets `refs/heads/dev`/`refs/heads/main`, resolving the runner from repo-local first, then the global skill path `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
3. **Feature branches unblocked:** a test push to a feature branch is not blocked by the suite (runner never invoked; worklog sync and branch-policy/context-budget checks still apply).
4. **Docs:** the install step is documented in this repo's developer docs (new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` + pointer from `AGENTS.md` per Q2) and is idempotent (safe to re-run; `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL` or equivalent bypass).
5. **Verification/regression:** a committed shell check or runner-driven assertion drives a simulated `dev` push (stdin) and a feature-branch push; asserts the gate refuses a deliberately failing suite (verified once, then reverted) and that feature-branch pushes skip the suite.
6. **Standard:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Standard:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** infrastructure/tooling only — no proxy code changes.
- **No repo-local `skill/` tree in llm** — the v3 hook as written in SorraAgents hard-fails on every dev push here; the runner must be resolved via the global skill path (same fallback pattern the context-budget gate already uses for `measure_context.py`).
- **SorraAgents policy** (docs/dev/context-budget.md, SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM) deliberately gives non-SorraAgents projects the v2 hook **without** the full-suite gate — extending llm's hook to v3-equivalent diverges from that documented convention and needs producer sign-off (Q1).
- **Worktrees:** `implement.py finish` pushes from a worktree; `core.hooksPath` is common-config so one setting covers all worktrees of this checkout, but a fresh clone/wiped `.git/config` loses it → installer must be re-runnable (idempotent).
- **No cross-repo edits without authorisation:** repo boundaries — `skill/`, `command/`, agent-infra dirs in SorraAgents are out of scope for an LP item without explicit direction (affects Q2).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Push timeout vs cold-suite duration:** `implement.py finish` pushes with a 600 s default timeout (`_resolve_test_timeout` → `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand`; llm has no override); on timeout it kills the whole process group and raises `PushTimeoutError` — the code explicitly anticipates the pre-push hook's `run_tests.py` outliving the parent. A cold ~4300-test full suite may exceed 600 s on this host, making the gate backfire on the first push after the cache expires (2 h TTL, git-state fingerprint). **Mitigation (recommended):** provision a sensible per-command timeout (or pre-warm the suite cache) in the same work item; verify with a timed simulated push. The 2 h cache makes repeat pushes cheap.
- **Cache location in worktrees:** pushes originate from worktrees; the runner writes `.worklog/cache` under its invocation repo. Implement's post-push/audit consumers read main-checkout `.worklog/cache` — a worktree-cached run may be invisible to them unless run cwd/cache resolution matches (verify; may need to run the gate from the main checkout or confirm the runner resolves the repo root consistently).
- **`--strict-git-env`:** the runner refuses to run when repository-override env (`GIT_DIR` etc.) is present; if any wrapper injects these, the gate would hard-fail or need `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP`. Verify in the simulated push.
- **Divergence from framework policy:** extending the llm hook to a v3-equivalent full-suite gate contradicts the documented sibling-project convention (SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM gives siblings v2 without the suite gate). Producer sign-off required (Q1); if declined, AC2 cannot be met by a hook-only fix and the alternative (framework-side change in `implement.py finish`) is a SorraAgents-scoped item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no proxy code changes; the `.githooks/post-*` hooks and `worklog-post-pull` are out of scope. Any discovered framing improvements (e.g. installing the hook on sibling repos, updating SorraAgents docs table) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** `implement.py finish` pushes without `--no-verify` (verified — no `--no-verify` in the push path), so an active hook gate applies to framework pushes, not just manual ones.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` committed (v2, file mtime 2026-08-31): worklog pre-push sync (branch `refs/worklog/data`), protected-branch policy (`main`/`master`/`HEAD`), context-budget regression gate (F6) — **no** test gate.
- `git config core.hooksPath` → unset; `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `*.sample`).
- Global test runner present: `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (the runner `/skill:test` uses; supports `--scope full --strict-git-env`, and caches results per git state in `.worklog/cache`).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` exists in llm (total 967) — context-budget gate is satisfiable.
- llm has no `docs/dev/release-process.md` (the dev-push-gate docs live in SorraAgents); llm has `docs/dev/` with other analysis docs.
- `.git/config` `[core]` section shows no `hooksPath` line; repo has ~82 worktrees sharing the common config.

## Desired change

1. Add a scope-aware full-suite gate to llm's `.githooks/pre-push` (v3-equivalent): read stdin once, capture push targets; `need_full_suite` when `remote_ref` is `refs/heads/dev|main`; run the runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env --json`; refuse the push on failure; skip tests for feature-branch pushes (matching SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 semantics). Runner resolution: repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` first, then global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (mirrors the existing `measure_context.py` resolution); fail behaviour on "no runner found" per Q3.
2. Idempotent installer (`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`): set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`; leave committed hooks untouched (never overwrite); `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1` bypass.
3. Docs: new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (install, verify: `git config --get core.hooksPath`; simulate dev push via stdin) + pointer from `AGENTS.md` (per Q2).
4. Verification test: a shell check or runner-driven assertion that a simulated `dev` push invokes the gate and a feature-branch push skips it.

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-push` — add scope-aware full-suite gate (v3-equivalent with global-runner fallback)
- `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` — new idempotent installer (sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, skip flag)
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — new developer doc (install, verify, bypass knobs) (location per Q2)
- `AGENTS.md` — pointer line to the hook install doc (location per Q2)
- Reference: SorraAgents `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, canonical gate implementation) — read-only reference, not to be edited from an LP item

## Related work

- SorraAgents SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push integration gate (the design this item implements for llm).
- SorraAgents SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61 — scope-aware test gate (v3 hook).
- SorraAgents SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM — per-project hook-variant selection (siblings ship v2, no suite gate) — the policy Q1 asks to extend.
- SorraAgents SA-0MT1WPMFY002N71Z — v2 pre-push hook with context-budget gate (source of llm's current hook).
- LP-0MUFJQ8ON009URQL — completed `[test-failure]` for `test-pre-push-hook.mjs` (SorraAgents hook test; confirms v3 semantics: dev push without repo-local runner hard-fails).
- LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W — completed item on committed symlinks causing duplicate/inconsistent test collection in worktrees (caveat against a `skill/` symlink approach for runner resolution; prefer global-path fallback).
- Duplicate check performed (2026-10-20): `wl search` for `pre-push`, `hooksPath`, `hook`, `test gate`, `dev-push` — no overlapping open/completed item covers llm's hook installation; proceed.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (OPEN QUESTION): **Where should the full-suite gate live for llm?** The committed llm hook is v2 (no test gate) and the v3 gate assumes a repo-local runner llm lacks. Options: (a) **Recommended** — extend llm's `.githooks/pre-push` to a v3-equivalent gate with runner resolution repo-local → global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; self-contained, satisfies all four original ACs. (b) Keep llm on v2 and instead fix `implement.py finish` (SorraAgents) to run the full suite before pushing — contradicts SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81's deliberate deferral and is cross-repo. (c) Symlink/create a repo-local `skill/` tree and install the unmodified v3 hook — risks duplicate test collection (LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W) and ships a framework tree into llm.
- Q2 (OPEN QUESTION): **Where are the install docs published?** llm has no `docs/dev/release-process.md`; gate docs live in SorraAgents. Options: (a) **Recommended** — new `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` + `AGENTS.md` pointer in llm (self-contained, satisfies "documented in developer docs" within repo scope). (b) Update SorraAgents `docs/dev/context-budget.md` project table + rollout section — cross-repo edit under an LP item; needs a SorraAgents work item. (c) Both.
- Q3 (OPEN QUESTION): **Fail behaviour when the test runner cannot be found on a dev/main push** (e.g. fresh machine without pi skill install). Options: (a) **Recommended** — fail-closed (refuse the push), matching v3 semantics and the ticket's "deterministic" intent; deterministic gate, at the cost that a machine without the global skill cannot push to dev until it runs the installer. (b) Fail-open with a loud warning (mirrors the context-budget gate's fail-open when `measure_context.py` is absent); keeps pushes working but re-opens the incident's hole on un-provisioned machines.

## Effort and risk (pre-decision estimate)

- **Effort: M (medium).** Rough WBS for the recommended option (Q1a): hook gate edit (~80 lines shell, mirroring v3), installer script (~30 lines), 1 shell/runner-driven verification test, docs (~1 page) → O=2 h, M=4 h, P=8 h.
- **Risk: Medium.** Drivers: (i) cold full-suite duration vs the 600 s push timeout (highest-impact unknown — a slow gate could break every `implement.py finish` push); (ii) divergence from the documented sibling-project hook policy; (iii) cache visibility from worktrees. Mitigations: timed simulated push with a provisioned `timeoutPerCommand`, keep the `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` escape hatch, choose fail-closed only after Q3.
- **Contingent on Q1:** option (b) (framework-side change in `implement.py finish`, SorraAgents) is out of LP scope and would be a separate cross-repo item; option (c) (repo-local `skill/` symlink + stock v3 hook) raises the risk to High given the known duplicate-collection defect (LP-0MUHOHP82006NT3W).
- **Confidence:** 60% on effort, driven by the unresolved timeout question. Re-run `/skill:effort-and-risk` after Q1–Q3 are answered (script requires stage `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MUFJQ8ON009URQL** – [test-failure] tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs::BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP=1 bypasses the policy check — failing test (completed)
- **LP-0MV7WUEJW0033UAN** – Close coverage gap: **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (completed)
- **LP-0MRNV040H0055N2Q** – [test-failure] test_stub_router_integration — flaky test-ordering-dependent assert ok Failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, ac2, acceptance, acs, active (+339 more)

# Gate the `models.compact` summarizer dispatch through the provider budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Problem

`models.<name>.budget` (LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV) makes the free-tier request-budget
behaviour configurable per model. That only works for requests that go through
the provider fallback chain in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.

`models.compact` is the exception: `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
(`build_compact_summarizer()`, `_compact_model_config()`, `_remote_chat_url()`)
resolves the chain itself and calls each provider entry **directly over httpx**,
bypassing `localhost:8080`. It therefore never reaches
`acquire_provider_budget()`, so a `models.compact.budget` block — or an entry
`rate_limit_rpm` on a `compact` provider — has no runtime effect. The
per-model-tuning goal explicitly names `compact` as a chain the operator wants
to tune, so this gap is material.

## Decision required (OPEN QUESTION 1)

The intake text allows two mutually exclusive routes; the ACs are already
written conditionally, so the plan below is concrete for **option 1** and
collapses to two doc edits + one doc-assertion test for option 2.

1. **Gate the summarizer dispatch** (recommended): call the budget gate before
   each summarizer tier attempt. A summarizer call has no session affinity, so
   it is always treated as a *new* session — pass through to the next tier
   rather than wait, honouring the per-model `budget` block.
2. **Document the exemption**: state in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and
   `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` that `models.compact` is not budget-gated, that a
   `budget` block there is inert, and drop `compact` from the stated tuning
   scope.

**Why option 1 is recommended:** the item title, and ACs 1, 2, 4 and 5, all
presuppose gating (only AC3 is option-2); the parent item's goal (user story)
explicitly names `compact` as a chain to tune, and option 2 permanently removes
it from that scope. Option 2 is also 1–2 hours of work against a real functional
gap, so it is the cheaper-but-lossy route.

**Entanglement:** this item came out of the parent's OPEN QUESTION 1
(`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — accept the split, or widen the parent and absorb this
item). If the producer picks "widen the parent", this item is closed as
absorbed; if "accept the split" is chosen, option 1 here is the intended
resolution. Do not implement before that answer lands.

## Facts established at planning (2026-10-20, code inspection)

- **The summarizer is synchronous.** `_summarizer()` (proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py:794) is
  called synchronously by `plan_session_compaction` (proxy/proxy/compaction.py:825),
  which is reached from the **async** `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`
  (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2617) — never from a worker thread.
- **The gate is async.** `acquire_provider_budget()` (proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py:413) is
  `async def`, and its limiter call
  `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment` (proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py:35)
  takes an `asyncio.Lock`. It therefore cannot be awaited from the sync
  summarizer; `asyncio.run()` inside a running loop raises, and the lock is
  loop-bound, so spinning a fresh loop per call is unsafe.
  → Implementation note (supersedes the intake's literal call signature): add a
  **synchronous, no-wait** sibling primitive in `provider_budget.py` (e.g.
  `try_acquire_new_session_budget()`) that reuses `reserved_slots()` /
  `new_session_limit()` / `_provider_rpm()` — the *new-session* case only, no
  waiting and no affinity. It is safe without the async lock because the
  summarizer call already blocks the event loop for its whole duration (sync
  httpx), so no other task can be inside the limiter's critical section.
- **Tier fall-through already exists.** The chain loop calls
  `resolve_provider(compact_cfg, failed_provider=..., config=config)`; on a gate
  denial set `failed_provider = name` (exactly as the failure path does at
  compaction_summarizer.py:855) so the next tier is chosen and the denied entry
  cannot be re-selected. Note `resolve_provider` also excludes the named
  provider's **failure domain**, so a denial on one opencode entry can skip its
  siblings — the same rule the failure path already applies, and the reason the
  denial must be recorded in the diagnostics.
- **Attempt diagnostics do not exist on this path.** The normal fallback path
  records `_record_attempt(..., status="rate_limited", reason=..., limit_rpm=...,
  effective_limit=..., reserve_slots=..., remaining=...)` into a `diagnostics`
  list surfaced in the 503 payload (proxy/proxy/provider.py:7139/7156 via
  `_build_exhausted_response`). The summarizer only logs
  `compact summarizer provider=%s failed (%s)` and returns
  `EmptySummary(kind, attempts)`. AC2 therefore needs a small per-tier
  diagnostics list (e.g. `EmptySummary.diagnostics` plus a
  `_record_compact_attempt()` helper) carrying provider, status, reason,
  `limit_rpm`, `effective_limit`, `reserve_slots`, `remaining` **and** the
  resolver's effective source layer (delivered by the parent item).
- **Shipped config is inert today.** `models.compact` declares no
  `rate_limit_rpm` and no `budget` block (proxy/config.yaml, `compact:` section
  ~line 866+), so AC4's fail-open case is the current production behaviour.
- **Shared bucket.** A summarizer dispatch consumes a slot in the same
  per-provider-entry window as interactive traffic (the bucket is keyed by
  entry, never by model — the parent item's explicit constraint). Enabling
  `rate_limit_rpm` on a `compact` entry therefore lets `compact` and
  `plan`/`author`/`code` starve each other; that is the intended design, not a
  defect.

## Blocking dependency

`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` (layered `models.<name>.budget` resolver) is
**plan_complete but not implemented**, and its own `needsProducerReview`
question is unanswered. AC2 (honour `models.compact.budget`, expose the source
layer) cannot be met until that resolver exists, so this item must not be
implemented first. Dependency edge wired in this planning session.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Option 1: a gated `compact` provider entry is skipped, not dispatched, once
   its `rate_limit_rpm` window is full — no HTTP request is issued to that entry
   and the summarizer advances to the next tier; when every tier is gated it
   returns an `EmptySummary` (falsy `""`) with `kind="rate_limited"` and the
   full tier count, without raising.
2. Option 1: `models.compact.budget` values are honoured for the summarizer
   dispatch (the new-session semantics of `reserve_ratio`, `wait_max_seconds`,
   `max_waiters`, `affinity_ttl_seconds` apply and the call never waits), and the
   per-tier attempt diagnostics record provider, status, reason, `limit_rpm`,
   `effective_limit`, `reserve_slots`, `remaining` and the effective source
   layer.
3. Option 2: `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` state that the
   summarizer bypasses the budget gate, and `compact` is dropped from the stated
   tuning scope. (Vacuous if option 1 is chosen.)
4. Behaviour is unchanged when no `rate_limit_rpm`/`budget` block is configured
   on the `compact` chain: identical POSTs, identical order, identical timeout —
   fail-open.
5. Tests cover the chosen behaviour. Option 1:
   `proxy/tests/test_compaction_compact_summarizer.py` (gated skip +
   fall-through, all-tiers-gated `EmptySummary`, no-config fail-open,
   diagnostics contents) plus `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (the sync
   decision path: allowed/denied and reserve maths parity with the async path).
   Option 2: a test asserting the documented exemption.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Write the failing tests: `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` for the sync
   new-session decision primitive (deny at the window edge, reserve maths,
   ungated entry, never waits) and
   `proxy/tests/test_compaction_compact_summarizer.py` for gated-skip +
   fall-through, all-tiers-gated, and the no-config fail-open case (AC1, AC4,
   AC5) — the existing `COMPACT_CONFIG` fixture and `_run()`/`_make_client()`
   helpers make these cheap to add.
2. Implement the sync no-wait primitive in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
   (reuse the existing reserve/limit helpers; no affinity, no waiting).
3. Call it before each tier POST in `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`; on
   denial record the diagnostic, set `failed_provider = name`, continue to the
   next tier (AC1).
4. Add the per-tier diagnostics to the summarizer's failure result and the
   warning log; include the resolver source layer once the parent lands (AC2).
5. Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (summarizer section — gated, new-session
   semantics, never waits, shared per-entry bucket) and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (`rate_limit_rpm`/`budget` also apply to `compact`).
6. Run the suite through the test skill.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py` — gate call in the `_summarizer` tier
  loop; per-tier diagnostics; `EmptySummary` kind on full denial.
- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — synchronous no-wait new-session decision
  primitive alongside `acquire_provider_budget()`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — only if `resolve_provider` needs an explicit
  excluded-names set instead of `failed_provider` (see Risky assumptions 3).
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_compact_summarizer.py` — gating behaviour, the
  authoritative test module for `build_compact_summarizer`.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — sync decision path + reserve parity.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — documentation.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — only if a commented `budget`/`rate_limit_rpm` example is
  added to the `compact:` chain (no shipped value change).

## Risky assumptions / prototype needed

1. **Sync gate without the async limiter lock.** Success = a targeted test
   proves a gated `compact` call inside a running event loop neither awaits the
   lock nor raises, and the slot accounting matches the async path. If it does
   not hold, fall back to threading the gate decision into the summarizer from
   the async caller.
2. **Effort.** Autoplan rates this Extra Small/Low; the real slice (new sync
   primitive + diagnostics + docs + two test modules) reads **Small**. Re-estimate
   at implementation.
3. **Denial scope.** Excluding via `failed_provider` also excludes the entry's
   sibling failure domain. If per-entry-only skipping is wanted, the loop needs
   an explicit excluded-names set — decide (and test) at implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the summarizer call `acquire_provider_budget()` directly, as the
  intake text says? Answer (this session, code inspection): no — it is `async`
  while the summarizer call path is synchronous (`compaction.py:825` inside
  `evaluate_and_apply_compaction`), and the limiter's `asyncio.Lock` is
  loop-bound. Final: add a sync no-wait sibling primitive in `provider_budget.py`;
  AC intent unchanged.
- Q: Do the summarizer attempt diagnostics exist that AC2 refers to? Answer
  (this session, code inspection): no — the compact path has only
  `EmptySummary(kind, attempts)` and a warning log; the diagnostics list AC2
  names is the normal-path `_record_attempt()`/`diagnostics` structure
  (`provider.py:7139/7156`). Final: mirror that shape on the compact path.
- OPEN QUESTION 1 (option 1 "gate" vs option 2 "document the exemption") —
  directed to the producer. Why it matters: it selects the whole implementation
  (code + docs vs docs-only) and interacts with the parent's unanswered
  split/widen decision. Recommended: option 1. See "Decision required" above.
  Planning completed on the recommendation without applying it.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-20 (plan session `herdr-1792457759-126109-11084`): auto-plan skip path
  (effort Extra Small / risk Low) — the six automated review stages were run
  against the existing content; added the Decision/OPEN QUESTION 1 section, the
  code-inspection facts (sync summarizer vs async gate, existing tier
  fall-through, missing attempt diagnostics, inert shipped config, shared
  bucket), the blocking dependency edge to `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`, a test-first
  implementation order, `**Key Files:**`, risky assumptions and this Appendix.
  Tightened AC1/AC2/AC5 to name their observables and test modules; no AC was
  removed or added. No child items: a single deliverable slice (XS plan path).

# Intake brief: make local GPU utilisation/prefill metrics visible to the usage report

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy usage report to measure **local prefill time**
(dispatch → first byte) alongside decode time, so "GPU busy %" reflects real slot
occupancy and large local prompts stop being invisible.

## Problem statement

`report.md` currently reports `Local model utilization → Busy time = 7h 02m (29.3%)`
and `Total compute (slot-time) = 7h 47m`, derived by pairing **local `Stream
started` → `Stream finished`**. That window starts at *first byte*, so the entire
prefill/prompt-processing phase is excluded.

For large local prompts, prefill is the dominant cost. In the same 24h window
(2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23) the proxy logged `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for
every one of the **463** local requests:

| Prefill (dispatch → first byte) | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Samples | 463 |
| p10 | 3.3 s |
| **median** | **61.8 s** |
| p90 | 269.8 s |
| max | 817 s (13.6 min) |
| **Sum** | **14.3 h** |

Examples: `dispatch_first_byte_ms=98697.8 cache_state=warm cached_ratio=0.942` and
`dispatch_first_byte_ms=133126.9 cache_state=cold cached_ratio=0.000` (212 cold /
251 warm in the window). Adding 14.3 h of prefill to 7 h 47 m of decode puts real
occupancy near **79,500 s ≈ 46% of 48 slot-hours**, versus the 16% the report
implies. This directly misleads capacity work (slot count, ctx size, queue
tuning) — including the concurrent slot-count investigation.

Corroborating gaps in the same report:

- `## Decode speed` and `## Prompt eval speed` are **empty** ("No llama-server eval
  timing samples in window"), so there is no independent decode/prefill evidence.
  `llama-server.log*` in the window contains no `eval time` lines (older rotated
  files do, e.g. `llama-server.log-2026-10-07.gz` has 296) — ingestion or build
  verbosity likely regressed, and that must be established.
- The report's TTFT table is dominated by remote samples; local `ttft_seconds` is
  never logged (only `dispatch_first_byte_ms`).
- The prefill phase is observable in the proxy already: 11,050
  `lease_extended_during_prefill` events with `progress=None`, i.e. prefill polling
  works but exposes no numeric progress.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy-usage-analysis` computes and reports **local prefill time** per local
   stream from `dispatch_first_byte_ms` (falling back to the pairing of dispatch
   and first byte when absent), including p10/p50/p90/max and the **window total**,
   with an explicit statement that the figure is slot-time, not wall-clock.
2. `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the union of
   **dispatch → finish** intervals (prefill + decode), with the decode-only figure
   retained alongside as a separate row, and a labelled lower/upper bound. Existing
   fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals.
3. A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report (slot-seconds and % of
   slot-time each), so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes.
4. The empty decode/prompt-eval sections are fixed or explained automatically:
   determine why no llama-server eval-timing samples exist in the current window
   (`llama-server.log` verbosity / build / rotation) and either restore ingestion
   or have the report print a named, self-diagnosing reason (log path, files
   scanned, lines matched) instead of an unattributed blank.
5. Unit tests cover: the prefill parser, the union-interval busy calculation
   (including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams), the fast/cheap split on
   the new intervals, and the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path. Fixtures are
   copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy` lines (`dispatch_first_byte_ms=`).
6. A regenerated report for the same window shows the corrected busy figure and
   the new prefill/decode split, with the numbers in this brief used as the
   expected-order sanity check (≈14.3 h prefill, ≈7.8 h decode).

## Risks / notes

- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` is logged per local request but is **not** identical to
  `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` (queue wait is split out as `queue_wait_ms`); define
  which interval maps to slot occupancy and document it.
- Unfinished/aborted local streams (2 in the window) have no `dispatch_first_byte_ms`;
  they must be reported as "unknown prefill" rather than silently dropped.
- Changing "busy" semantics changes historical comparability; keep the old
  decode-only number visible and state the definition change in the report header.
data.title: Make local GPU busy/prefill metrics visible in the proxy usage report

# Run the controlled N=3 (and N=4) slot-count sweep in a quiet/maintenance window

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the measured N=3/N=4 sweep that
`LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` could not complete on shared production, so the
concurrency-vs-capacity projection (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes;
N=3 ~6.7%) is validated or refuted against real local TTFT, decode speed,
queue-timeout rate and VRAM.

## Why this exists

The deterministic analysis in `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`
(AC1/AC2/AC4) is complete and recommends **keep N=2** pending this sweep. The
AC3 measured sweep was attempted on 2026-10-20 against the live proxy while it
was serving 5 concurrent sessions (52 distinct sessions / 5 min, 2 audits + 4
herdr panes holding local leases). Every benchmark turn-1 request stalled at
600–760 s (1200 s timeout) and llama-server stopped answering health probes, so
the run was aborted, the harness restored the config (sha256 `6eec5656…`) and a
controlled `start-proxy.sh --restart` returned the proxy to healthy (N=2,
`--parallel 2`).

## Task

Run the sweep in a window with no other local-lease holders (drain or stop
herdr panes / audits), using the same harness as the prior verdict
(`LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7` / `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`):

```
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --sweep --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
# then, if memory permits:
LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm \
  python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark \
  --slots 4 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 \
  --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>
```

Record per N: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, llama-server
startup + `--parallel` agreement (must match `session_slot_pool_size`), per-slot
KV memory and system MemAvailable. Then update the decision in
`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (or a successor doc) and,
if the verdict moves to N=3/N=4, create the config-change item that also
re-decides the warm-threshold = 95%-of-per-slot target (which becomes 79,121 at
N=3 vs 120,627 at N=2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A sweep run at N=2, N=3 (and N=4 if memory allows) with the harness above,
   with the results committed under `proxy/benchmarks/results/`.
2. The run records `--parallel` agreement, per-slot context clamp, and system
   MemAvailable, and explicitly notes any validity caveat (live leases, remote
   fallback) as the prior verdict did.
3. A recorded verdict (keep N=2 / move to N=3 / N=4) that reconciles the
   measured queue-timeout and denial rates with the concurrency projection in
   the reevaluation doc.

## Risks / notes

- N=3 clamps per-slot context to 83,285 (warm threshold 79,121); N=4 to 61,440.
- Prefill is serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), so more slots add
  decode concurrency, not prefill capacity.
- Do **not** run this against the shared proxy during active multi-agent work.

## Goal

Explain the +96% growth in logged (paid-serving) token volume between 2026-10-18/19 and 2026-10-20/21 — 421.7 M → 828.5 M tokens while requests fell 29% (12,810 → 9,137, i.e. ≈2.8× tokens per request) — and decide whether it is intended context growth, a context-budget regression, or an accounting artefact.

Discovered from: LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (verification of LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX — off-peak low-priority fallback). The verification could **not** attribute the rise to that epic, but nothing currently owns the trend.

## Evidence already gathered

24 h windows measured with `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` (log clock = local Europe/Dublin, UTC+1):

| | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions / requests | 217 / 12,810 | 228 / 9,137 |
| Logged tokens (input+output) | 421.7 M | 828.5 M |
| Tokens per request | ≈32.9 k | ≈90.7 k |
| Token share by serving entry | `opencode-go-3` 99.98%, `-2` 0.02% | `-3` 99.36%, `-2` 0.20%, `deepseek-flash` 0.44% |
| Local streams | 910 | 576 |
| `munitoai-free` + `munitoai` entry lines | 14,555 | 5,967 |

Notes: only opencode/deepseek streams emit a `tokens=prompt/completion/total` triple — local and `munitoai-free` streams do not — so "logged tokens" are **paid-serving** tokens and the free-tier share must be read from counts, not tokens. Candidate causes to separate:

1. Genuine context growth (bigger sessions/prompts) — check `start_context_size` / `max_context_size` distributions in `standard_sessions.csv` for the two windows.
2. A context-budget / compaction regression — the window contains compaction/context-budget changes (`c443240c`, `f496626e`, `42f93580`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`) and a proxy restart at 2026-10-20 13:10 local.
3. Accounting artefact — `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events) did not exist pre-change; confirm it is not double-counting or re-attributing tokens.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three candidate causes are each ruled in or out with a quantified comparison of the two windows (`start_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages` distributions from `standard_sessions.csv`/`low_priority_sessions.csv`, and per-stream token triples).
- AC2: The tokens-per-request increase is attributed to a named cause with supporting numbers, or explicitly recorded as unexplained with the residual quantified.
- AC3: Any regression found is either fixed here (with a regression test) or filed as a child work item with the blocking relationship recorded.
- AC4: A durable cost metric is proposed (or implemented) so this drift is detected without an ad-hoc before/after session — e.g. a tokens-per-request trend in the daily proxy-usage report.
- AC5: Findings are commented on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO so the verification record carries the resolution.

## Evidence commands

```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --start "2026-10-18 14:37:48" --end "2026-10-19 14:37:48" --output-dir /tmp/cost/base24
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --start "2026-10-20 14:44:27" --end "2026-10-21 14:44:27" --output-dir /tmp/cost/post24
# per-session context distribution
python3 -c "import csv,collections,statistics as s; rows=list(csv.DictReader(open('/tmp/cost/post24/standard_sessions.csv')));
r=[int(x['max_context_size']) for x in rows if x['max_context_size']]; print(len(r), s.median(r), s.mean(r))"
```

### Implementation notes — model/entry `budget` blocks (option (a) as specified)

**Scope implemented: exactly the ACs as written** (AC1–AC9, with AC7 already narrowed by the plan to the two real fallback entry points). That is option (a) — "accept the split" — the plan's preferred resolution of OPEN QUESTION 1. No OPEN QUESTION was widened here: gating the `models.compact` summarizer dispatch remains `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (still blocked) and this item does not touch `compaction_summarizer.py`.

**What landed**
- `provider_budget.resolve_budget_settings(provider_cfg, config, model_config)` resolves each of `reserve_ratio`, `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters`, `affinity_ttl_seconds` per knob through **entry `budget` > `models.<name>.budget` > `server.*` > built-in default**, returning `BudgetSettings` plus a `sources` map (`entry`/`model`/`server`/`default`).
- `BudgetDecision.sources` / `.source_label` expose provenance as `knob@layer` (e.g. `reserve_ratio@model`). Log lines and the diagnostics attempt entry append `budget_source=…` **only** when a model/entry block supplied a value, which is what keeps AC3 byte-identical for the shipped config.
- `acquire_provider_budget()` gained a `model_config=` keyword; both fallback entry points pass their request's model config (AC7), and both record a `budget_source` field on `rate_limited` / `rate_limited_waited` attempts (AC6).
- `_maybe_record_provider_affinity(..., model_config=...)` records affinity with the **model-resolved** TTL, so the recorded lifetime matches the chain that created it (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`). Lookup needed no change: the stored expiry is already absolute.
- Existing single-knob helpers (`wait_max_seconds`, `wait_max_waiters`, `reserve_ratio`, `affinity_ttl_seconds`, `reserved_slots`, `new_session_limit`) keep their signatures and now delegate to the resolver, so every existing caller/test is unchanged.
- Docs: `proxy/config.yaml` (header block + commented `budget:` example on `plan:` + server-knob cross-reference), `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (entry field table + model-level block), including the shared-bucket boundary and the `compact` caveat.

**Assumptions documented**
1. **AC4 (out-of-range vs malformed).** The Desired-change text says values are "clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today (ratio to [0,1], wait/TTL to >= 0, malformed values fall back to the default with a warning)", while AC4 says out-of-range values "fall back to the next layer". Implemented as: **unparseable values fall through to the next layer with a warning; out-of-range values are clamped into range with a warning** — i.e. today's clamping semantics are preserved at every layer and only malformed input falls through. Both cases are logged, neither raises nor blocks a request, and tests cover both per key. This keeps "clamped exactly as the server-level knobs are today" true.
2. **Log byte-identity (AC3)** is achieved by emitting the provenance suffix only when a model/entry block contributed; server/default-only configs (including the shipped `config.yaml`) produce the exact previous format — pinned by a test that asserts the full skip line verbatim.
3. **No model *quota*** was introduced: the limiter bucket stays keyed by provider entry, proven by a test where two models with different `budget` blocks exhaust one shared `rate_limit_rpm` window.
